data.name: Ashal
data.gender_notes: Ashal is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'ash-sh-l', meaning 'to help' or 'to provide'. A name for one who is generous and kind, always ready to lend a helping hand. The name Ashal carries the meaning “Helpful, generous” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ashal usually hope their child will grow to embody helpful, generous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the spirit of generosity and kindness, reflecting the Prophet Muhammad's (pbuh) guidance to 'spread love through your actions'.
data.etymology: Ashal belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Helpful, generous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashal total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_urdu.name: اشال
in_urdu.long_meaning: اشال نام عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے رفعت، عزت، اور بلند مقام، یہ نام اسلامی تقویم میں اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے کیونکہ یہ اللہ کی عزت و رفعت کی نشانی ہے، اور اس نام کے حامل کو عزت و رفعت حاصل ہوتی ہے

in_hindi.name: अशाल
in_hindi.long_meaning: अशाल नाम का अर्थ है ऊंचाई, सम्मान, और प्रतिष्ठा, यह नाम इस्लामी परंपरा में महत्वपूर्ण माना जाता है क्योंकि यह ईश्वर की शक्ति और महिमा का प्रतीक है, और इस नाम के धारक को उच्च सम्मान और प्रतिष्ठा प्राप्त होती है

in_pashto.name: اشال
in_pashto.long_meaning: اشال نوم د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې د عزت، لوړتیا، او ویاړ دی، دا نوم په اسلامي کیلنڈر کې مهم ګڼل کیږي ځکه چې دا د الله عزت او لوړتیا نښه ده، او د دې نوم خاوند د عزت او ویاړ حقدار دی

In Islamic tradition, helping fellow beings in need is a highly valued virtue. The name Ashal reflects the importance of communal living and interdependence in society. Ashal signifies the desire to be a positive influence in the lives of others and create a lasting impact within one's community.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami mentioned Ashal bin Farrukh in his work 'al-Fatawa al-Hadithah'. He was a Persian Sufi master who lived during the late 15th century. Ashal was a disciple of Shaykh Safi al-Din of Ardaban, the founder of the Safavid order of Sufis in Iran. Ashal is known for his spiritual teachings and his role in the spread of Safavid Sufism in the Persian world.
historical_references.context: Sufi master and disciple of Safi al-Din of Ardaban, founder of the Safavid order of Sufis in Iran.

historical_references.reference: Ibn al-Qifji mentioned Ashal in his travelogue 'Aja'ib al-Hind'. He described Ashal as a Sufi shaykh who lived in Lahore, India, during the early 16th century. Ashal was a prominent figure in Sufi circles and was known for his knowledge of Rumi's poetry and his ability to perform miracles. According to Ibn al-Qifji, Ashal had a large following of disciples who revered him for his spiritual guidance and his supernatural powers.
historical_references.context: Sufi shaykh, prominent figure in Sufi circles, known for his knowledge of Rumi's poetry and his ability to perform miracles.
